title: connect_ws lowercase-only scheme check — correct for SSRF prevention
description: connect_ws checks starts_with('ws://') || starts_with('wss://') (lowercase only). This is intentional: the comment explains that accepting only lowercase ensures the guard and tungstenite see the same string — no risk of tungstenite rejecting an uppercase scheme after the guard passes. RFC 3986 §3.1 says schemes are case-insensitive, so WS:// would be technically valid. However, no real JMAP server will advertise WS://, and case-folding the input before checking would require allocating a normalized string. The strict check is the right tradeoff.
